The tragedians more frequently used it of tears: see Thes. vol. 6 p. 1033.

if the author wanted to call the tears of the fatherland μητρός πηγήν [the mother's spring], as the scholiasts interpret it, he has spoken very absurdly, as I showed in Philologus vol. 16 p. 218.
